curriculum.lesson_evidence: Food safety is the set of habits that keep harmful microbes from reaching the food someone eats. A hazard is anything that could make food unsafe, such as dirty hands, a raw-meat drip, or food left warm for hours. A control is the action that reduces that hazard. Year 7 students start by naming the hazard before they choose the control, because a tidy bench is not the same thing as a safe process.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
A student sneezes over a plate of cut fruit, then says the fruit is fine because it looks clean. Name the hazard and one control.

FEEDBACK
Hazard: droplets from the sneeze can land on ready-to-eat fruit. Control: throw that fruit away or compost it, wash hands, and cut a fresh piece. Looking clean does not remove contamination.

WATCH FOR
Thinking food is safe whenever it still looks and smells normal. Many unsafe changes cannot be seen.
